title: Vendor approval policy & technical preflight - BlueLayer Analytics
summary: Procurement-led intake to align MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, and technical preflight for a private/VPC deployment. Discussed approval matrix, billing path, KMS options, and a short benchmark pilot. Agreed on next steps: share security pack, provide draft billing SOW, schedule on-prem network preflight with firewall/egress team.
topics: Pricing approval flows and finance signoff
Private deployment checklist (VPC peering, egress, KMS)
action_items: Sophie Ramos - Send security pack (SOC2 + ISO summary + DPA draft) - due 2025-03-12
Daniel Kim - Run preliminary latency/cost estimate for BlueLayer's 75 rps peak - due 2025-03-14
Maya Patel - Share BlueLayer procurement approval matrix and target pricing band - due 2025-03-11
Ethan Wu - Provide network diagrams and egress policy for preflight - due 2025-03-13
next_steps: Redwood to send security + compliance artifacts and DPA annotated draft
Schedule technical preflight (SE + BlueLayer network team) week of 3/17
Redwood to produce a 2-week pilot SOW and estimated billing path for finance review
Customer to confirm decision committee attendees and timeline by 3/11
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-08
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Ramos (Redwood AE); Daniel Kim (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (BlueLayer - Procurement); Ethan Wu (BlueLayer - Security Engineer); Lena Ortega (BlueLayer - Head of Platform); Noah Greene (BlueLayer - Finance)
-- Optional links referenced: security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack), draft DPA (link: https://redwood.example/dpa-draft), pilot SOW template (link: https://redwood.example/pilot-sow)

[00:00] Sophie Ramos: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Patel: Maya here, procurement.
[00:08] Ethan Wu: Ethan, security.
[00:09] Lena Ortega: Lena, platform.
[00:11] Noah Greene: Noah from finance.
[00:13] Daniel Kim: Daniel, SE at Redwood.
[00:15] Sophie Ramos: Great. Objective for today is to align on the MSA/DPA redline priorities, confirm the SLA and pricing workflows, and plan a short technical preflight for VPC and egress. We'll keep it tight 30-45 mins.

[02:05] Maya Patel: To frame procurement, our gate is finance + security signoff. We have a three-week procurement window but pricing needs to be in the ballpark today so we can route approvals. We do have a couple must-haves: strong audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS integration or escrow, and a clear SLA credit formula.

[03:10] Sophie Ramos: Understood. On the audit logs and SSO we're SOC 2 aligned and support SAML/SO for SSO — sorry SAML/SAML? (laughs) I mean SAML/ OIDC — transcript error — but yes we have SAML and OIDC. We can share the SOC 2 summary and an ISO extract.

[04:00] Ethan Wu: For KMS, we prefer customer-managed keys in our VPC model. Is that supported? We want to ensure logs and keys never leave our tenancy.

[04:20] Daniel Kim: Short answer: yes for Dedicated/Private we support customer KMS via BYOK integrations. For hosted there are options but for the strictest controls we recommend Private (VPC / on-prem). I will caveat that some models have additional constraints for KV cache handling and you cannot hold the runtime key locally in all cases — we'll put the precise mapping in the security pack.

[06:15] Lena Ortega: We have concerns about egress fees and cross-region traffic — our platform is multi-region and we need predictable billing. How do you structure egress and token billing for a dedicated/private pilot?

[06:38] Sophie Ramos: For Dedicated/Private, billing is typically a mix: reserved capacity fee plus per-token or per-inference unit. Egress (cloud networking egress) is generally passed through if we operate in your cloud account; for Redwood hosted we absorb baseline egress but large cross-region transfer can incur fees. We'll include a sample billing scenario in the SOW.

[08:10] Noah Greene: Finance wants a clear decision tree: if usage goes above committed throughput, what's the overage rate, and do we have a cap? Also need month-to-month vs annual commit options documented for approvals.

[08:35] Sophie Ramos: We'll provide 3 pricing bands in the SOW: monthly burst, 6-month pilot commit, and 12-month reserved capacity with discounted unit rates. Overage rates and soft caps can be configured; we'll put explicit rate tables.

[10:05] Maya Patel: Back to the DPA: there are a couple of sections we will push back on — subprocessing and data retention. We need the retention window spelled out per dataset and a clause for data residency.

[10:30] Daniel Kim: We typically allow customers to set retention or opt-in for prefix/KV cache persistence. For private deployments you can set 0 retention for KV caches; for hosted we have default retention, but redlines are common — we'll flag the DPA where this is configurable.

[12:20] Ethan Wu: On SLA, BlueLayer requires 99.9% uptime on critical inference routes and a latency SLO of 200 ms p95 for short prompts. Do you have those guarantees for private?

[12:45] Daniel Kim: For Dedicated we can target 99.9% with SLA credits defined; p95 200 ms depends heavily on model choice and sequence length. If you choose a smaller model family or a quantized variant, it's achievable. We'll propose two SLO profiles in the SOW — "low-latency" and "cost-optimized" — with explicit tradeoffs.

[14:00] Lena Ortega: We will likely want a canary routing policy and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if downstream systems detect regressions. Is that supported?

[14:20] Daniel Kim: Yes, our rollout tooling supports canary and fallback policies. We'll include an ops-runbook for rollbacks and for tracing regressions to prompt sets.

[15:40] Maya Patel: For procurement pathing, who needs to sign the MSA? Usually our legal wants pricing spelled inside an SOW attachment and the MSA to be high-level. We also need clarity on liability caps and indemnity for data breaches.

[16:10] Sophie Ramos: The standard approach is MSA + SOW where pricing and SLAs live in the SOW. On liability caps, we can follow an enterprise template — we need to know BlueLayer's risk appetite. We can surface typical liability bands and cyber insurance requirements in the security pack.

[18:05] Noah Greene: Quick question on escrow: do you offer code or model escrow for on-prem or private deployments? It's a procurement ask for certain regulated customers.

[18:30] Sophie Ramos: We have an escrow path for customers with very specific requirements — that's usually an enterprise add-on and we can discuss with legal. We'll note that in the draft.

[20:15] Ethan Wu: Network-wise, our preflight will check that your runtime can be reached via VPC peering and that gRPC endpoints are allowed. We also need to validate your certificate rotation process.

[20:40] Daniel Kim: SE note: we'll need a short network checklist from BlueLayer — subnets, NAT gateways, firewall rules, service account permissions. We'll run a connectivity test during the technical preflight.

[22:12] Lena Ortega: On timeline, if we get the annotated DPA and SOW this week and finance signs off, we could start a 2-week pilot by end of March. Is that realistic?

[22:40] Sophie Ramos: Yes, that's the aim. We'll aim to get the security pack + DPA and a draft SOW in your inbox by 3/12. With your network diagrams we'll schedule the preflight for week of 3/17.

[24:55] Maya Patel: A couple of redlines we will most likely require: (1) data residency clause especially around EU data, (2) deletion certificates on request, (3) audit rights.

[25:20] Daniel Kim: We'll flag those items with engineering and legal. For deletion certificates — we can provide attestations for data wiped from Redwood-managed caches. For private deployments, it's straightforward since everything is in your tenancy.

[27:00] Noah Greene: About the pilot billing: can you provide a capped estimate for the 2-week benchmark? We need a ceiling to approve.

[27:20] Sophie Ramos: We'll give a capped pilot estimate and also a not-to-exceed for egress. Daniel will model expected token costs using your sample throughput numbers — Maya, you said 75 rps peak?

[27:40] Maya Patel: Yes, roughly 75 rps peak with an average prompt size of 120 tokens.

[28:10] Daniel Kim: Noted. I'll run the math and include a conservative margin. Expect the estimate by 3/14.

[30:05] Ethan Wu: One small note — we may ask for a temporary limited SOC 2 report or readout for the pilot. How quickly can you provide that?

[30:20] Sophie Ramos: We can share the SOC 2 type II summary and the control matrix this week. Full report typically requires NDA in some cases but summary docs are fine.

[31:45] Lena Ortega: On the operational side, who will be the point of contact at Redwood for post-pilot onboarding? And what's the escalation path?

[32:00] Sophie Ramos: I'll be AE primary, Daniel will be SE primary. For ops and SRE we have an onboarding owner; we'll include contact names in the SOW. Escalation goes AE -> SE -> SRE -> Customer success director depending on severity.

[33:40] Maya Patel: For the DPA redlines, we'll send annotated comments by Wednesday. Is that timeline okay?

[33:55] Sophie Ramos: Perfect. That helps us route items to legal quickly.

[35:10] Noah Greene: Can we get a simple spreadsheet comparing model variants, expected latency, and cost per 1k tokens? Finance needs that side-by-side.

[35:30] Daniel Kim: Yes, I have a benchmark template; I'll fill it in with small/medium/large variant numbers and quantized options. I'll include memory and GPU footprint notes.

[37:05] Sophie Ramos: Quick recap and next steps — we'll share: (1) security pack + DPA draft by 3/12, (2) pilot SOW and capped estimate by 3/14, (3) schedule technical preflight for week of 3/17 once we receive network diagrams. BlueLayer will: (a) send procurement matrix and annotated DPA by 3/11, (b) provide network diagrams by 3/13, (c) confirm decision committee list by 3/11.

[39:00] Maya Patel: Sounds good. One ask — can you include a sample SLA credit calculation in the SOW? Procurement will need that to evaluate risk.

[39:20] Sophie Ramos: Yes we'll include explicit credit formula and examples.

[40:10] Lena Ortega: Minor point — we may need to scope for model pinning per environment. We don't want silent model upgrades.

[40:30] Daniel Kim: We support version pinning and will include rollout controls in the ops runbook.

[41:05] Sophie Ramos: Great. If no further questions we'll close it there. Thank you, everyone.
[41:15] Ethan Wu: Thanks.
[41:17] Maya Patel: Thanks all.
[41:19] Lena Ortega: Bye.
[41:20] Noah Greene: Bye.

End of transcript.
